method: Manual normative review, compiler/runtime inspection, and MLIR regression evidence. This inventory is not a full conformance certification.
z3: Pinned in-process Z3 4.13.4 for compiler bit-vector analysis and parameterized Boolean sampling plans; native and WASM runtimes bind parameters and sample exact ranks without linking or calling Z3.

features.detail: Every numbered subsection is represented; open implementation items remain explicit.
Reviewed against compiler preparation, generated checkers, and runtime search.

Compiler Z3 proves static plans. Native and WASM compiled-plan samplers complete ordinary and explicitly ordered packed integral residuals of arbitrary aggregate width with live captures, frozen bits, domains, block masks and optimal soft priorities. State-array and queue foreach over complete hard integral semantic domains through 2^20 assignments uses generated rank traversal, including sparse wide enums and fixed enum arrays. Weighted, other runtime-foreach and non-integral paths retain limits.
Commit occurs only on a successful solve; pre_randomize side effects are independently observable.

Exact compiler Z3 plans and tables are uniform. Ordinary native/WASM integral residuals use compiler-generated Boolean plans, exact model counts and arbitrary-precision rejection-sampled ranks, including live captures, frozen bits, domains, block masks and optimal soft priorities. Hard runtime foreach over state arrays and queues uses complete semantic-rank reservoir sampling through 2^20 assignments, so solution gaps and unequal companion completion counts do not bias legal tuples. Soft, cyclic, ordered, function-priority and randomized-container foreach combinations, larger domains and non-integral forms remain open.
Packed integer domains and arbitrary-width rand bit vectors are executable.

Named enumerators, anonymous and typedef inventories retain arbitrary-width two-state representations in class and scope plans. Compiler Z3 analyzes exact membership; wide literal-pool records feed the Boolean sampler in native and WASM execution. Frozen nonmember enum state remains legal; conflicting source domains are diagnosed. Frozen semantic-pattern validation uses deterministic radix ordering for equal masks and a shared-prefix compiler Z3 proof for mixed masks, independently of user constraints; solver-free builds bound pair checks linearly and diagnose unproven domains.
Entire packed bit patterns are legal; nested enum members do not restrict the aggregate domain.
The LRM disallows rand and randc packed tagged unions; frontend validation applies to source declarations. Legacy synthetic IR domain support is not a language feature.

features.feature: Unpacked arrays, queues, and associative arrays
features.detail: Fixed unpacked arrays of packed integral elements use exact logical bitstreams for class and scope randomization, including multidimensional, descending, ascending and negative ranges. Enum domains and live modes apply independently to each element. Ordinary state-selected fixed-array paths compile to balanced Z3 selection plans with frozen X/Z and precise guard masks. One-dimensional dynamic arrays and queues retain specialized plans. Fixed integral randc arrays through 32 bits per leaf retain independent exact histories, including multidimensional and static storage. Dynamic container histories and modes, non-integral leaves, generalized selected-path function ordering and associative arrays remain incomplete. Fixed integral arrays also contribute their singular members to inside sets in ordinary constraints and expanded function bodies, including frozen wildcard symbols.

features.feature: Unpacked structs with member rand qualifiers
features.detail: Instance and static unpacked structure properties contribute only explicitly rand/randc qualified fixed integral leaves and rand/randc fixed integral arrays, recursively through qualified structures. Ordinary members retain strings, nested state and X/Z symbols. Integral randc leaves through 32 bits, including fixed arrays, have independent persistent cycles; static cycles and modes are shared across instances. Whole-structure, leaf, nested-structure, array-element and class mode operations compose with temporary explicit property selection. Qualified scalar real members use numeric-coordinate plans and preserve ordinary shortreal state. Dynamic container and class-handle members, and structures in recursively randomized objects remain incomplete.

Source class and scope plans admit scalar real and shortreal properties, qualified real structure leaves, and real leaves in finite active object graphs. Compiler Z3 emits finite numeric-coordinate relations with spacing-weighted cells, subnormals, signed zero and clipped finite extremes. Live IEEE bounds, promoted shortreal comparisons, soft preferences, constraint/rand modes, explicit property lists, checker-only calls and transactional failures execute in native and WASM at O0/O3, in native and bytecode tiers. Frozen properties retain original NaN/infinity payloads rather than decoding coordinate placeholders. Captured binary64 bounds use deterministic round-to-nearest, ties-to-even binary32 cell parameters; targets validate their full source precision and never link or call Z3. Typed backend arithmetic, integral-to-real conversions, selection and rank decoders remain available. Numeric integral casts and $rtoi now lower to compiler Z3 relations with halfway-away rounding, truncation, arbitrary-width low bits, nonfinite four-state unknown planes and exact binary32-to-binary64 numeric provenance through selection and negation. MLIR validates adjacent IEEE candidate payloads, 1/32/130-bit results, active source point and bounded-interval casts including zero and wide large values, frozen nonfinite casts, integer-to-real candidate solves, X/Z-to-zero conversion, and payload-preserving IEEE system-call round trips. Native $rtoi uses integer IEEE truncation operations that also execute in bytecode. Universal Z3 proofs cover all binary32 and binary64 inputs at widths 1, 8, 32, 64 and 130, plus exact binary32 promotion. Computed FP arithmetic numeric casts now extract sanitized IEEE payloads before the proven bit-vector conversion kernel. The pinned compiler Z3 tactic exposes its existing local deterministic completion option; unreachable NaN completion functions do not enter the sample plan. Additional universal compiler-plan equivalences cover every raw binary32 and binary64 arithmetic-result encoding at widths 1, 8, 32, 64 and 130 with rounding and truncation. Typed MLIR covers addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and intermediate rounding before 1/32/130-bit casts; source MLIR covers live addition captures, active real points, zero, half ties, checker-only calls and transactional failures. Arithmetic payload-bitcast plans remain incomplete. Sampler branches propagate mandatory literals before expanding arithmetic cofactors, restoring all inputs in the exact diagram so counts, projections and weighted intersections retain their original relations. Each Boolean gate computes a constant-time flag identifying whether positive AND traversal can reach a random literal, so other arithmetic skips propagation. Active real/shortreal point and bounded-interval integral casts execute in native and WASM; general full-coordinate arithmetic efficiency remains incomplete. MLIR covers the 18.4.1 numeric-density example, every comparison in both operand orders, malformed wire formats, aliases, parent/descendant global constraints and null guard sifting. General full-coordinate arithmetic efficiency, real arrays, joint real/integral distributions and complete real probability semantics remain open.
Finite acyclic type graphs, polymorphism, aliases, nulls, and descendant constraints are supported; recursive type graphs remain incomplete.
Values may repeat; enabled properties are committed together.
Shared class storage and shared mode state are planned.
Integral semantic domains up to 2^32 values and 32-bit representation use a keyed bijection.

Compiler-admitted scalar and fixed-array source constraints now use one compiled relation and one shared cyclic operation to project exact legal domains, permute dense ranks and persist canonical managed snapshots. Live bound, block and inline changes, including unconstrained transitions, restart changed legal domains without scanning sparse declared ranges. Keys, positions, snapshots, fields and RNG are published only after the final ordinary solve succeeds. Native and WASM MLIR cover instance and static sharing, checker and frozen modes, shallow copy, wide ordinary fields and weights, reordered plans with different completion counts, zero weights and failure atomicity. Fixed multidimensional array leaves and qualified enum/integral members retain independent shaped histories, including static sharing, shallow copies, element modes and frozen X/Z. Source constraint-context changes that preserve the legal domain, runtime foreach combinations, function-priority stages, dynamic-container histories and object aliasing remain open.

Integral cyclic fields through 32 bits, including fixed array leaves, qualified structure members and sparse signed enums, are sampled sequentially from projected legal domains before ordinary fields. One shared compiled-plan cyclic operation serves every stage; only the final solve and successful commit publish histories and RNG. Native and WASM cover joint cycles, 130-bit ordinary fields, live modes, explicit selection and failure atomicity. Function-priority stages, dynamic-container histories, object aliasing and source constraint-context changes with equal legal domains remain open.

features.feature: Randc real and dist on randc
features.detail: Forbidden by the language; existing diagnostics cover dist and width restrictions.

Total packed expressions, arithmetic, bitwise operators, inside, concatenation, constant replication, and conditional expressions are compiled to MLIR and solver programs. Fixed unpacked inside-set arrays descend to integral leaf selections before compiler Z3 planning, preserving multidimensional declaration coordinates and candidate relations. Reusable pure template graphs preserve shared intermediates and wide literals through both compiler Z3 decoders, with instruction generation proportional to graph nodes and uses. Immutable value slots preserve exact widths and hard/soft boundaries in scalar and wide target interpreters; each candidate refreshes its slots. Compiler value/X/Z plane construction retains shared operands instead of cloning expression trees. Candidate checks bind shallow lowering templates and reuse each plane node within one evaluation; fresh evaluation banks preserve candidate bindings and control-flow dominance. A 96-element four-state membership set emits 2794 instructions and agrees with native and bytecode semantics across frozen symbols, mode changes, consuming casts, wildcard absorption and inverse solving.

Variable and state division/remainder, signed integral exponents, Table 11-4 parity and reciprocals, wide operands, and undefined-result planes are compiled into Z3 sampling plans. Uncoerced undefined values fail, while two-state casts and known absorbing bits retain LRM arithmetic semantics. Disabled four-state scalar properties, fixed-array elements and qualified structure leaves bind their stored unknown symbols through compiler captures masked by the live active-bit inventory. Candidate checks use the pre-solve snapshot; active random candidates remain two-state. Packed bit-selects and constant or variable indexed part-selects preserve separate value, X and Z planes, including computed operands from admitted functions, concatenation and undefined arithmetic. Widened signed address arithmetic retains declared coordinates and both indexed directions without truncation. Case, wildcard equality and integral inside use exact symbol planes, including frozen properties, typed ranges, known absorbing matches and active argument stages. General system functions and non-integral selections remain open.
Effective block inventories and individual mode bits are preserved.
Resolved extern bodies participate in Z3 planning, reusable templates, effective inherited constraints, and generated native/bytecode checking.
An implicit prototype without a body is treated as an empty constraint, as required by 18.5.1.
An explicit extern block without a resolved body is diagnosed. Effective pure declarations require a concrete implementation.
Base-first class inventories apply effective overrides and the 2023 extends marker.

features.feature: Soft priorities across inherited and contained objects
features.detail: Derived and inline priorities are handled; all cross-object ordering cases need verification.

Constant and state-valued two-state integral endpoints, explicit weights, default ranges, and additive overlapping items have executable plans. Constant endpoints retain intermediate conversion widths and signedness.

Self-determined integral weights are zero-extended, including negative signed bit patterns. State weights and weights computed from the distributed target or its explicit solve-before predecessors retain arbitrary-width unsigned values.

The compiled-plan sampler preserves each integral item's original mass after clipping and filtering. Exact target projections and arbitrary-precision normalization support state-valued endpoints, wide weights, overlapping items and noncontiguous defaults. Integral weights computed from the distributed target or its explicit solve-before predecessors export one Boolean root per bit and use exact unsigned bit masses with the original item denominator. Captured := range cardinality scales the expression before sampling. Expression targets, unresolved companion weights, candidate-dependent endpoints and real ranges remain open.

features.feature: Nonzero weights never make an otherwise legal solve fail
features.detail: The compiled-plan sampler's policy removes 64-bit mass overflow and bounded-domain traversal failures for admitted fixed integral distributions; full 2^64 ranges and arbitrary-width unsigned captures are covered. Target- and explicitly ordered predecessor-dependent weights retain exact positive support, including zero exclusions, negative signed bit patterns, checker-only calls, mode changes and transactional failures. General expression targets, unresolved companion weights, unresolved activation and function-priority stage combinations remain diagnosed. Source cyclic projection also retains exact positive support of ordinary distributions, including candidate weights, 130-bit captured weights, live support changes and zero-total-weight transactional failures.

features.feature: Soft dist and dist with solve before
features.detail: The compiled-plan sampler retains or discards soft distributions in global soft-priority order and samples whole distributed targets conditionally on earlier solve-before layers. State guards, earlier candidate guards and integral weights computed from those explicitly ordered predecessors are supported. Candidate-dependent zero soft weights can be discarded without constraining hard support. Split-target ordering, unresolved companion weights, unresolved candidate activation and independent function-priority stage combinations remain open.

features.feature: Multiple active distributions on one target
features.detail: The compiled-plan sampler combines per-value masses from every enabled distribution on admitted direct integral targets, preserving legal intersections even for incompatible requested marginals. General expression targets and real distributions remain open.

features.feature: Dynamic endpoints, candidate weights, and real ranges
features.detail: State-valued two-state integral endpoints are captured at each call, clipped to the target domain, and combined with exact original := range masses. Default complement membership includes explicitly listed zero-weight items and supports a default-only distribution. Integral candidate weights computed from the distributed target or its explicit solve-before predecessors are compiled once into shared immutable temporaries and width-linear Boolean root exports. The target runtime binds captures and samples arbitrary-precision masses without Z3. Unresolved companion-dependent weights, candidate-dependent endpoints, unknown-plane state endpoints and real ranges remain open.

Integral singular values and fixed unpacked arrays or slices expand into pairwise leaf inequality before Z3 planning. Multidimensional arrays, ascending and negative bounds, fixed state-array leaves, singleton groups, and duplicate references are covered in class and scope randomization. Duplicate leaves retain their identity and make the solve fail. Real leaves and dynamically sized container operands remain incomplete.
Packed two-state implication is present in Z3 and residual programs, including soft guards.
Hard and guarded soft constraints retain conditional semantics.

Fixed foreach dimensions expand into ordinary predicates before Z3 planning and function dependency analysis; runtime iteration covers admitted one-dimensional dynamic arrays and queues. Complete finite hard state-container relations use uniform semantic ranks, including 130-bit enums, fixed enum arrays, live constraint modes and frozen leaves. Generalized runtime dimensions and staged combinations remain open.

Live size, declared iterator type, universal conjunction and empty-array identity are implemented. For complete hard integral domains through 2^20 assignments, generated mixed-radix traversal and reservoir sampling preserve uniform joint probabilities under state-array and queue exclusions, including sparse 130-bit enums, fixed enum arrays and frozen leaves. Finite semantic domains combined with cyclic, soft, function-priority, ordered or randomized-container stages remain diagnosed; larger domains retain their prior limits.

features.feature: Fixed, associative, string, and multidimensional foreach
features.detail: Fixed packed and unpacked dimensions, including multidimensional arrays, descending or negative bounds and omitted iterators, expand into typed constant-index predicates for class and scope randomization. Fixed state-array elements are captured per predicate. Z3 handles the resulting ordinary relation, live modes, soft preferences and explicit solve-before on integral elements. Associative, string, non-integral leaves and generalized runtime dimensions remain incomplete.

Fixed foreach is expanded before planning. State-selected fixed random-array elements use balanced compiler selection plans with exact leaf mode and dependency masks, including independent static sibling references. The Figure 18-3 algebra suppresses invalid accesses only through state FALSE/TRUE or disabled blocks. Signed, wide, unknown and out-of-bounds indices retain structural errors across two-state casts. Complete runtime-sized candidate solving remains open.
Selected dynamic array and queue reductions are lowered; all containers, methods, and with expressions are not covered.

Finite acyclic object graphs solve together with alias identity equations. Parent and descendant-owned constraints bind integral or IEEE scalar leaves by their static receiver paths, preserving frozen child state, null guard algebra, disabled blocks and transactional failure. Arbitrary recursive graphs, object arrays, non-rand receiver aliases and general unresolved access paths remain open.
Self edges and cycles are diagnosed; aliases and packed paths retain precise ordering masks.

Compiler Z3 tables and structural plans preserve ordering with arbitrary-width masks and projected keys. Native and WASM compiled-plan samplers count exact existential projections for integral bitstreams, including live captures, semantic domains, modes and optimal soft preferences; each projected value counts once regardless of its later completions. Version-2 ordering metadata carries multiword masks. Compiler and runtime DAG plans defer partially ordered fields to their latest legal layer and include unordered fields in the final joint group. Fixed integral array elements use the same exact masks and conditional probabilities; whole unpacked arrays and randc operands are diagnosed. Real ordering and state-dependent selected paths remain incomplete. Lowering hashes repeated edges, joins transitive overlapping bit views with per-bit adjacency and schedules their latest legal layers with one sink traversal. MLIR checks a 130-field chain, duplicate and multiple-operand edges, conditional versus joint sampling after mode changes, and overlap-induced cycle diagnostics.

Cyclic stages project exact hard legal domains before the ordinary solve, with later cyclic and ordinary bits existentially free. Ordinary solve-before edges and soft preferences are sampled only after cyclic values are frozen. MLIR covers mixed and joint cyclic fields, persistent live scalar and fixed-array domain changes, static sharing, copied histories, wide distribution support and transactional failure. Function-priority stages, runtime foreach combinations, dynamic-container and aliased-object histories, and source constraint-context changes with equal legal domains remain incomplete.
Class-wide storage is shared by every instance and inherited plans use the same storage.

Expression returns, blocking result assignments, nested calls, and virtual receiver dispatch are supported. Automatic statement bodies support packed locals and constants, typed initializers, blocking and compound assignments, mutable input copies, blocks, if/else, early returns, return-variable assignments and fallthrough. Executed unused initializers retain errors; state branch guards preserve procedural four-state truth. Persistent and nonlocal writes, const writes, and static result reads before initialization are rejected. Constant repeat loops and same-width logical right-shift for loops have exact expansions, including the LRM count_ones example, lexical break/continue, early returns, local reinitialization and standalone updates. Counts follow 12.7.2 after typed casts; negative/X/Z counts execute zero times. The policy is 256 iterations per loop and 4096 expanded bodies per call. Packed case, casex, casez and case-inside statements preserve first-match ordering, grouped labels, defaults, fallthrough, early returns and lexical loop exits. Comparisons use common width and signedness under 12.5, unbased literals fill the context, frozen and mixed random/state X/Z comparisons remain exact, and labels after an earlier match retain short-circuit error guards. Normal case consumes complete symbols; casex/casez ignore the designated symbols in either operand. Procedural ===/!== and ==?/!=? use distinct symbol comparison planes, including consuming result casts and 130-bit operands. Integral inside combines wildcard member and inclusive simple-range predicates with four-state OR, including dollar endpoints. Case-inside uses asymmetric wildcard membership and takes only known true comparisons, preserving first-match label evaluation. Nested selectors retain symbols and label-error guards through safe capture; empty live dependency masks remain state under nesting. General dynamic, larger and unbounded loops, dynamic-container membership, tolerance ranges and pattern cases, case qualifier reports, non-integral comparisons, non-integral locals, selected local lvalues, candidate-selected evaluation errors and other receivers remain incomplete. Fixed unpacked integral array members of inside and case-inside descend through every dimension before planning, with common numeric comparison context, frozen X/Z, live state and bidirectional direct membership constraints. Native function execution and compiled plans agree on wildcard absorption, unmatched left unknowns, two-state return coercion and first-match case behavior. Expression-return clones retain function-origin symbol semantics for legal procedural X/Z literals.
Random properties read only inside a function are frozen as pre-solve state; argument paths remain solver variables.

features.feature: Implicit function priority can shrink solution space
features.detail: Native and WASM compiled-plan samplers sample higher-only integral constraint sets independently, freeze accepted arguments, and allow lower stages to fail without committing assignments or sampler RNG. Source path masks preserve syntactic dependencies through simplification; guarded atoms retain separate stages. Explicit solve-before uses conditional projections within each function stage. Wide packed paths, soft priorities, live modes, frozen arguments and semantic domains are covered. Staged randc histories, aliased object identity, dynamic foreach and general procedural function evaluation remain open and are diagnosed.

Signedness casts, clog2, countones, onehot, onehot0, isunknown and countbits participate in compiler Z3 plans and native/WASM execution. Value, unknown and high-impedance planes distinguish X from Z in admitted packed operands. Countbits combines distinct control LSBs as a set of 0/1/X/Z selectors, including live four-state controls. Casts, shifts, concatenation, replication and conditional merging preserve Z as required; undefined arithmetic and unary arithmetic on X/Z operands produce X. Clog2 consumes unsigned value bits after X/Z-to-zero conversion, including active four-state random declarations. Snapshot captures preserve frozen symbols through mode changes and checker-only calls. Scalar, 130-bit and bidirectional 32-bit MLIR regressions cover these cases. Computed packed bit-selects and constant or variable indexed part-selects retain exact X/Z counts after expanded function argument stages, concatenation, bitwise operations and undefined arithmetic. Non-integral bitstreams and system functions outside the admitted integral set remain open. Live and candidate count targets reuse one prefix sum with linear construction work rather than enumerating all cardinalities. Equal partial counts share cofactors; a 65-bit equality/inequality plan emits 2,064 Boolean nodes. MLIR checks cover every count, signed out-of-range targets, frozen modes, joint counts, consuming three-bit casts and 130-bit targets whose high bits cannot alias legal counts.

Scope randomization shares class expression and automatic statement-body function validation, packed path priority analysis and compiled-plan stages. Module/package and other non-instance functions support nested calls, actual-argument priority, frozen body state reads, output/ref restrictions, cycle diagnostics, packed locals, branches, early returns and 130-bit results. Finite repeat and right-shift loop bodies use the same one-way stages, including stateless static-lifetime functions and std::randomize calls. Packed case, casex, casez and case-inside statements share class first-match expansion, typed comparisons, state error guards and 130-bit return handling. Instance receiver plans, general loops, dynamic-container membership, tolerance ranges and pattern cases, case qualifier reports and other general function bodies remain incomplete. Fixed unpacked integral array members of inside and case-inside descend through every dimension before planning, with common numeric comparison context, frozen X/Z, live state and bidirectional direct membership constraints. Native function execution and compiled plans agree on wildcard absorption, unmatched left unknowns, two-state return coercion and first-match case behavior. Expression-return clones retain function-origin symbol semantics for legal procedural X/Z literals.

Integral state predicates and handle comparisons are evaluated safely before solving, including null and bounds checks. Unknown-plane predicates outside admitted integral normalization and non-integral solving remain open. State-selected function body branches validate only the selected arm, including executed unused initializers. Procedural unknown truth is false; a known one bit remains true.

The complete Figure 18-3 truth tables are implemented with safe compiler captures and hard creation-validity predicates in native and WASM solving. Only state TRUE/FALSE suppress errors; RANDOM cannot hide them. Null handles, handle comparisons, fixed/state dynamic array and queue bounds, known invalid random-array slices, state-selected fixed random-array elements with exact live dependency masks, state tagged-union arms, guarded body errors, disabled blocks and frozen variables are covered. Unused function inputs retain evaluation errors and source RANDOM classification. Live guard reference and argument masks preserve independent Z3 function-priority stages after sifting. Computed packed selections and variable indexed part-selects preserve unknown address errors across consuming casts; partial out-of-range selections fail unless a state guard or disabled block discards them. General candidate-dependent accesses, other mixed unknown-plane predicates and complete runtime-sized foreach encoding remain open.
Up to 64 preferences use lexicographic satisfiability in Z3 and residual evaluation.
Guards belong to the predicate while target reference collection examines the soft expression itself.
Later declaration, derived class, and inline preferences receive higher priority.

Static foreach expansion preserves declaration-order iteration so later body instances receive higher soft priority, including descending ranges. Full object-containment and runtime-iteration relationships still need coverage.

Direct identifiers and fixed integral paths discard only earlier directly referencing preferences, including unused function inputs. Enclosing guards and indirect function body reads do not trigger a disable.

features.feature: Live block modes and conditional disable
features.detail: The generated checker and narrow/wide runtime programs honor block masks and if/implication guards; Z3 uses the all-enabled planning state.
Derived and inline preferences after a disable remain active.
Dynamic selections, unpacked paths, and foreach disable targets are not covered by the fixed path matcher.
Randomize and hook plans dispatch through the concrete class selected for a handle.

features.feature: Randomize return status and atomic property commit
features.detail: Successful solves return one; failed or null-receiver calls return zero without property commits.
Ordinary draws work; randc behavior with arbitrary cycle-domain changes needs additional tests.
Pre runs before state capture; post runs after a successful commit and is skipped on failure; graph aliases invoke hooks once.
Finite graphs are supported; recursive and generalized container graphs are incomplete.
Effective constraints, properties, and hooks are resolved against the selected concrete class.

features.feature: Inline constraints merge with class constraints
features.detail: Inline hard constraints intersect the effective class formula; inline soft preferences have higher priority.
Frozen lookup inventories distinguish randomized receiver members from enclosing scope captures.
Frontend bindings preserve local:: and enclosing lexical scope through constraint preparation.
Queries and setters retain mode state; disabled variables are fixed and not committed.

Fixed unpacked integral arrays have persistent per-leaf mode bitmaps, including multidimensional subarray setters, arbitrary leaf counts, static sharing, and inherited dynamic-class resets. Disabled four-state leaves preserve X/Z on commits and bind their original unknown planes into admitted integral constraints, including conversion and known absorbing operators. Only singular leaves may be queried. Fixed randc array leaves, including qualified and static members, retain their independent histories when frozen or omitted; explicit array selection temporarily activates every leaf. Dynamic array and queue modes and histories remain open.

With compiled-plan samplers, finite integral partial selections use exact projected counts with frozen bits, including sparse wide constraints and fixed array element masks. Frozen four-state symbols use snapshot captures and active-bit masks without a runtime solver. Complete hard state-container foreach domains through 2^20 assignments use uniform rank traversal, including unnamed frozen enum values and fixed wide enum leaves. The optional build without compiler Z3 retains bounded fallback search; non-integral and generalized dynamic-container relations remain open.
Masks control hard/soft predicates and ordering edges; disable-soft uses the live mask too.
Mode-sensitive residual checks are correct within their bounded domain, but capture-free proofs do not remove general runtime completeness limits.
State captures are evaluated for each call; mode masks select the live formula.

Persistent exact domain snapshots restart scalar and fixed-array instance, qualified structure-member and static cycles after live legal-domain changes, including state bounds, constraint modes and inline or unconstrained transitions. Static histories are shared across instances; failed solves and disabled fields retain prior history. Equal-domain source context changes, dynamic-container histories, aliased objects and generalized function-priority stages remain open.
Listed non-rand values become random temporarily; unlisted properties remain state; persistent mode state is preserved.
Packed values and static fields work; non-packed selected values retain planner restrictions.
Hooks and constraint checks run on current values, with no random draws or property writes; post runs only on success.
Up to 64 automatic, formal, static, package, and design values can be selected.

Packed integral, enum, packed aggregates and fixed unpacked arrays of integral leaves work. Ordinary state indices select exact array paths, including 65-bit elements and multidimensional logical bitstreams. Complete finite hard foreach over state arrays and queues preserves uniform scope tuples, including gapped legal domains. Bounds failures preserve all scope assignments. Randomized dynamic containers, class handles and non-integral aggregates remain incomplete.
Variables and the process stream are committed only when the solve succeeds.

sections.title: Adding constraints to scope variables—std::randomize() with

features.feature: Scope with constraints and zero arguments
features.detail: State captures, hard/soft constraints, disable-soft, and current-state checking use the same solver plan.
Fixed member offsets are encoded as logical extraction in Z3 and the residual program.
Direct ordering works within finite limits; user function plans and general selected paths are incomplete.

sections.title: Random number system functions and methods

features.feature: Process and object random API family
features.detail: PCG state and bounded draws have native and bytecode implementations.

features.feature: Urandom unsigned return and optional seed
features.detail: $urandom supports zero arguments and an optional integral seed. Explicit seeding replaces both PCG state words with the same canonical mapping as process::srandom, so equal seeds determine equal sequences across independently inherited thread streams, including negative 32-bit seeds and repeated seeding.
One or two bounds, reversed bounds, and full-width endpoints use rejection debiasing.
Manual reseeding preserves stream independence and does not draw a value.
Exact object and process RNG snapshots are serialized.
Restores exact snapshots and future stream output.

Scope initialization streams, static and dynamic process streams, and object streams are independent. Lexical module/interface/program/package ownership is preserved through native and bytecode startup.

features.feature: Independent initialization RNG for each scope instance
features.detail: Each module/interface/program/package semantic owner has a distinct RNG seeded with the configured default. Static initializers and process registration resume that stream; optional $urandom(seed) arguments remain supported.
Processes and objects have explicit independent state.
Forked processes and bytecode tasks split the parent stream in lexical creation order.
Root-spawned static processes split their declaring scope initialization RNG independently of unrelated scopes; dynamic children still split their running parent.
New objects split the creator stream. Shallow copies preserve RNG state, modes and cyclic histories under 8.12 without reseeding the copied stream.
Synchronous static declaration initializers bind their lexical initialization RNG with no active logical thread. Class creation consumes that stream directly before static processes are created.
Object and process srandom plus snapshots allow deterministic replay.
Each weight is evaluated once; summation uses maximum operand precision with modular overflow.
No branch and no RNG draw occur when the total is zero.

Arbitrary-width integral weights use unsigned self-determined summation at maximum operand precision. Generated MLIR forms a significant-bit mask and rejection-samples complete ranks with the process RNG, including partial final words, tiny dynamic totals and modular overflow.

Finite grammars support typed rule-local return values, input/output/inout/ref arguments, defaults, and nested grammars in native and WASM execution. Recursive activations and generalized rand join remain incomplete.
Unspecified weights are one and explicit integral weights are evaluated on production entry.

Compile-time operand widths and alternative counts determine an exact natural-sum width, removing the 64-bit overflow limit. Arbitrary-width nonnegative integral weights retain proportional sampling, default and zero alternatives, and once-only production-entry evaluation. Negative signed values and X/Z weights are diagnosed before conversion or selection.
Finite grammar production conditionals lower to control flow.
First matching case and default rules are represented in finite production control flow.
Repeat counts and loop control are represented in the frozen grammar.
Current support covers shallow finite production items; generalized nested interleaving and bias remain incomplete.

Void and typed returns terminate the current production, and break aborts the current grammar without exiting an enclosing loop or grammar. Output and inout arguments copy back from inner to outer activations. Recursive grammar frames remain open.

Finite productions support input/output/inout/ref bindings, declaration-scope defaults and captured output addresses. Typed return values use one rule-local slot or a [1:N] array in syntactic occurrence order, including conditional, case and repeated items. Native and WASM MLIR tests cover strings, 129-bit values, unpacked arrays, nested return chains, early returns, managed ref aliases and output copy-back on grammar abort. Recursive activation frames and generalized rand join still limit grammar execution.
